title: var on lambda parameters, and running a source file

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does the compiler make of the lambda `(var s, Integer i) -> s.repeat(i)`?

options.text: It accepts it and infers the type of s from the target
options.says: The page says var cannot be mixed with explicit types in lambda parameters: all or none must be var.

options.text: It refuses it, since var and an explicit type are mixed
options.says: The page says you cannot mix var with explicit types in lambda parameters; all or none must be var.

options.text: It accepts it once both parameters carry an annotation
options.says: Annotations are why var is allowed on lambda parameters, but the page's rule is still all or none, annotated or not.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does `java Greeter.java World` do in Java 11?

options.text: Writes Greeter.class next to the source file, then runs it
options.says: The page says the launcher compiles in memory and no .class file is written to disk.

options.text: Runs a Greeter.class that javac must have built earlier
options.says: The page says the launcher sees a .java argument and compiles it itself, without an explicit javac step.

options.text: Compiles the source in memory and runs it, with no class file
options.says: The page says the launcher compiles the source in memory, runs the bytecode at once, and writes no .class file.

concepts: java Program.java compiles a single source file in memory and runs it, writing no class file.
var may be used on lambda parameters so they can carry annotations, but only when every parameter uses var.
